test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The weight of an object on the Moon is ______

options.text: may be greater than or less than depending on the density of the object
less than the weight on the earth
greater than the weight on the earth
equal to the weight on the earth

solution:
The correct answer is __**less than the weight on the earth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An object’s **weight** is the force exerted on it due to **gravity**.
 
• The Moon's gravitational force is about **1/6th** of the Earth's gravitational force.
 
• Thus, an object on the Moon weighs **less** than it does on Earth.
 
• This is because the **mass** of the Moon is much smaller compared to Earth, leading to a weaker gravitational pull.
 
• For example, an object that weighs **60 kg** on Earth would weigh only around **10 kg** on the Moon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **May be greater than or less than depending on the density of the object**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because the **weight** of an object is determined by the gravitational force, not its **density**.
 
• Weight is a force and is affected by gravity, whereas density is a property of matter and does not change with location.
 
 
 
• **Greater than the weight on the Earth**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect because the Moon's gravitational force is weaker than Earth's.
 
• An object cannot weigh more on the Moon compared to Earth due to the lower gravitational pull.
 
 
 
• **Equal to the weight on the Earth**__
 
 
• This is incorrect as the gravitational force on the Moon is not the same as on Earth.
 
• The weight of an object changes with the change in gravitational force.
